modules.title: Structure & Invariance
modules.question: Which objects, relations, and stable structures should a model represent?
modules.intro: Start with objects and relations: how can a model turn complex observations into structure useful for dynamics prediction? Ask whether that structure comes from architecture, learning objectives, or data, and under which changes it remains useful.
modules.scope: This module studies representational content and inductive biases. M2 examines its latent organization; M4 examines its actual use.
modules.connections: NRI and C-SWM offer entry points through interaction graphs and object representations. SPARTAN and Causal-JEPA connect structural choices to adaptation or latent prediction. Compare how object information is obtained, whether structure changes with context, and whether recovered relations improve prediction.

modules.title: Representation Geometry & Manifolds
modules.question: How is knowledge organized in latent space, and what does that organization do?
modules.intro: Study both the geometry that trained models develop and the effects of deliberately imposing geometric structure. Identify which question a paper addresses before connecting a geometric observation to model behavior.
modules.scope: Emergent geometry, imposed geometry, and task benefits are distinct claims. A projection can suggest a hypothesis; additional evidence is needed to establish its role.
modules.connections: Interpreting Physics provides an entry point into physical information in representations; SMDS offers a method for comparing geometric hypotheses; GRWM connects diagnosis to long-horizon prediction. Read them together while keeping their model families, supervision, and functional evidence distinct.

modules.title: Generalization & In-Context Learning
modules.question: Does success in a new environment come from knowledge reuse or learning new dynamics?
modules.intro: Understand reuse and adaptation by specifying what changes: object combinations, hidden environment parameters, dynamics rules, or observability. Then ask what information the context provides.
modules.scope: Environment recognition, dynamics learning, and state estimation can all affect performance. Benefits from a longer context do not alone identify the mechanism.
modules.connections: CaDM provides background on history-based context encoding. Context and Diversity distinguishes environment recognition from environment learning; Dynamics Are Learned connects trajectory geometry to policy adaptation. Dreamweaver adds a view of object and attribute composition.

modules.title: Knowledge Use & Task Abstraction
modules.question: Which information actually supports prediction, planning, and decisions?
modules.intro: Connect internal representations to behavior. Study what information a task needs and how predictions, plans, or learning tendencies reveal whether that information is being used.
modules.scope: Decodability, use, and task value require separate evidence. Whether an abstraction transfers to a new task depends on what it preserves.
modules.connections: What Has a Foundation Model Found probes world structure through inductive bias on new tasks. DINO-WM makes the representation-to-planning interface concrete. Denoised MDPs and Value Equivalence help specify which details of the world need to be retained.

modules.title: Reliability & Sim2Real
modules.question: Which model errors matter for decisions, and when is a model trustworthy?
modules.intro: Separate visual quality, physical prediction, and task performance. Physical extrapolation, closed-loop use, and paired real/simulated evaluations provide complementary views of reliability.
modules.scope: Performance within simulation, agreement in real-world policy rankings, and successful transfer are different forms of evidence. Identify the evaluation target and pairing protocol.
modules.connections: SIMPLER asks whether simulation can reliably compare real-world policies; Rethinking Sim2Real examines fidelity and transfer. Physical Law Perspective and World-In-World add physical testing and closed-loop evaluation.

modules.title: Exploration & Efficient Adaptation
modules.question: What experience should an agent acquire or reuse in an unfamiliar environment?
modules.intro: Study the selection and use of experience: which actions reveal useful information, when stored experience is worth replaying, and how those choices help subsequent tasks.
modules.scope: Parameter identification within a model class, learning missing mechanisms, active collection, and experience replay have different assumptions and costs.
modules.connections: Plan2Explore studies exploration before tasks are known; ASID connects interaction to identification; Poke and Strike focuses on task-relevant information; Curious Replay studies reuse. Compare the information each method values and the conditions under which it is useful.

modules.title: Pretraining & Scaling
modules.question: How do controlled insights connect to stronger models and larger datasets?
modules.intro: Use pretrained video models, end-to-end JEPA, and broadly applicable world-model learning algorithms to understand representations, dynamics, action interfaces, and planners. These systems can also provide platforms for smaller mechanism studies.
modules.scope: Large-scale representation pretraining and executable planning involve different stages. A shared algorithm does not imply one checkpoint that works in every environment.
modules.connections: LeWorldModel provides a small end-to-end route. JEPA-WMs component studies separate architecture, objective, and planning effects. V-JEPA 2 and DreamerV3 offer broader references for data and task scaling.
